Lines.Text: Screee—
A piercing ring filled their ears, accompanied by a sickening nausea, as though space itself were twisting.
P was the first to open his eyes.
Every joint screamed as if a giant wave had hurled him ashore.
Groaning, he forced his heavy eyelids up. Above him was nothing resembling the concrete ceiling of their ruined practice room.
...What the hell is all this?
The dazed words slipped from his mouth.
A circular wall of shelves stretched impossibly high above him.
Millions—tens of millions—of ancient books and scrolls filled them without end.
Hundreds of wooden stairways scurried along rails of their own accord, connecting one tier to the next.
There were no lamps. Yet it was far from dark.
Violet nebula dust streamed through the air like a galaxy of fireflies.
Open books and sheets of parchment beat their wings overhead like vast flocks of birds.
A library, dreamlike and overwhelming, where the laws of physics had ceased to exist.
(scrambling upright, looking around) Girls! Wake up! Are you all right?!
One by one, the girls stirred on the cold marble floor, wincing in pain.
(sitting up, clutching her head, deathly pale) Ugh... I'm going to be sick...
Everything was bending... Where the hell are we...?
(her legs giving out beneath her, trembling) P... What on earth is going on...?
(her legs giving out beneath her, trembling) P... What's happening...? The walls are all books...
(staring blankly up at the flying books) ...
Faced with an impossible world beyond human reason, they were overwhelmed by instinctive terror.
Then...
A clamor like a crowded marketplace reached their ears.
Hey! That well-ghost text in Section 3 doesn't have enough unresolved anguish!
Get some manuscript paper and put more grief into the emotional arc! Now!
Oh, damn it! It's due back today, and the whole plot's a mess!
Section 4 librarians, we need backup!
Excuse me! Coming through! Book cart!
P and the girls turned toward the noise. Beneath the library's otherworldly grandeur, its true face came into view.
Horned dokkaebi hurried past with carts piled high with books. Restless ghosts with grotesquely twisted necks floated along the shelves, putting volumes away.
A huge yogoe stretched out dozens of arms to snatch flying pages.
This immense library was a workplace in the middle of its busiest shift, every kind of spirit scrambling to do its job.
Amid the chaos, Hana slowly woke with her head resting in Jiwoo's lap.
(groggily) Mm... Jiwoo... Is the... prank show over...?
Hana blinked, unfocused.
Something large and pale floated directly in front of her.
A maiden ghost who had been shelving books tilted her head. Blood streamed from her scalp as she drifted close to Hana's face and peered down at her.
Oh...? A human who's still breathing...? How did you get in here...?
Hana's pupils shrank to pinpricks as their eyes met.
Her mouth opened and closed. Before she could even scream, her eyes rolled back and she fainted again.
(turning white, clutching Hana and trembling) H-Hana!
Aaaah! Go away! Don't come near us!
(pushing the girls behind him, stepping between them and the ghost) Back off! Stay away!
P braced himself, eyes bloodshot.
Cold sweat ran down his back. At any moment, he expected the gathered spirits and monsters to swarm them and tear them apart.
Just then...
Good grief! Coming through, coming through! And do watch the ink! Keep it off the floor!
A small, round figure bustled out through the crush of ghosts and yogoe.
A furry little yogoe in a neatly fitted waistcoat, with a gold-rimmed monocle over one eye.
Looking like a cross between an owl and a raccoon dog, the adorable creature trotted toward them carrying a thick ledger with a quill tucked inside.
(pointing his ledger at the maiden ghost) You! Section 2 librarian!
Why aren't you working? Section 2 is about to burst at the seams! Go and move some parchment!
Tch. Fuss, fuss, fuss. (She drifts away into thin air.)
The maiden ghost drifts away into thin air.
The monocled yogoe cleared his throat, then bowed formally to P and the wary girls.
My apologies for the fright. It's peak returns time, you see. Stories coming due all at once.
Barely a moment to breathe.
(bewildered) You... I mean, what are you...?
(adjusting his monocle) Mongu, Senior Library Assistant of Yeongyo Archive.
I trust your difficult journey hasn't left you too much the worse for wear.
The Director has been most eager to receive our honored guests. This way, if you please.
Mongu set off at a brisk little trot.
Still frightened, P and the girls held tightly to one another's hands and followed.
Hundreds of books drifted down either side of the corridor, brushing past in a violet glow.
Between the towering shelves, spirits glanced at them with interest.
Seoyun looked around in wonder. Mina, overwhelmed by the bizarre sights, kept her eyes half closed and clung to P's jacket.
At last, they reached the heart of the seemingly endless library.
An enormous pair of mahogany doors stood before them,
inlaid with a geometric butterfly design in gold.
Director. Your guests have arrived.
CREEEAK—
The heavy doors opened by themselves, revealing a spacious office where a violet nebula rippled gently.
A blood-red carpet covered the floor. Through an enormous window filling one wall, constellations unlike anything in the living world glittered as though they might spill into the room.
And at its center...
The Director, Moomyeong, stood with effortless elegance in his violet suit and white mask.
He removed his fedora, held it over his heart, and spoke in a low, dreamlike voice.
A difficult threshold to cross. You have done well, P. And you, my little birds.
(a deep violet light flashing behind his mask) To those whose every light has gone out: welcome to Yeongyo Archive. Your true stage awaits.
BANG—!
With Moomyeong's dreamlike welcome, the heavy doors closed firmly behind them.
At last, the first page of P and the girls' strange ghost story turned.
